races.name: Shamrock Enterprises Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing six-year-old with consistent placed form over hurdles on Good ground (two places from three similar-going runs); headgear (hood/tongue-tie combination) in place, 26 days between runs is fine, and Phillip Enright rides for a trainer with modest recent form — maps to sit handy and will appreciate the honest gallop but has yet to win over hurdles.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Punchestown last time despite some jumping errors over three miles, showing he handles the trip on a sound surface; first-time hood and tongue-tie add interest, and he has a chance if the jumping holds together here.

runners_data.name: Chasing Blues
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Gavin Cromwell returning from a massive 418-day absence, with only two hurdle runs on record and a fade-in-finish flag; very lightly exposed over hurdles and the lengthy layoff makes it hard to trust despite the yard's 3/35 14-day record.
runners_data.comment: Coming back from 418 days off the track, he came down at Killarney when under pressure and has plenty to prove after a lengthy absence; first-time hood is the angle but he is hard to back with confidence until he shows more.

runners_data.name: Colwyn Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for P J Rothwell who has shown modest form over this sort of trip on Good ground (two runs in similar conditions); Dylan Robinson takes the ride and he will press for the lead, but a pulled-up in recent form and no wins suggests he is likely to be a pace-maker rather than a winning force.
runners_data.comment: Tumbled two out at Downpatrick on his latest start, which overshadows an earlier third and gives him something to prove at the obstacles; effective at this sort of trip and on soft ground, though jumping confidence needs to hold up here.

runners_data.name: Ellis Brittle
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed five-year-old with unknown going preference and no hurdles form on record; the 7lb-claiming Jordan Canavan rides for a trainer with minimal recent runners, making this a genuine unknown quantity who is very difficult to factor.
runners_data.comment: By Order Of St George and related to a bumper and hurdles scorer on the dam's side, though the dam herself was well beaten; makes his debut here and, while the yard is capable, he is very difficult to assess first time out.

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained five-year-old with a placed record over further on Soft and Heavy ground, so the step up to 2m4f on Good is a query; Sean O'Keeffe is a competent partner and the Mullins yard hits form at 7/19 over 14 days, making this one of the more interesting unknown-style runners despite limited Good-ground evidence.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on these figures, Fou De Toi showed useful form in France and has the profile of a horse capable of better; effective at today's trip, he disappointed on his last outing but returns after a 90-day break and the drop in trip looks favourable.

runners_data.name: Great Entirely
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, five years old and trained by Paul Kiely; has gone on Good ground three times without winning and his form reads P-6-P-5, yet he will force the pace and his willingness to lead makes him a key tactical factor regardless of winning prospects.
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Kilbeggan latest, doing his better work late in the race wearing a tongue-tie and comfortably held, but the step back up to a longer trip today is a positive; effective at this sort of distance on a sound surface, though overall recent form is patchy.

runners_data.name: Lastofthenatives
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old whose most recent run ended in a pull-up (75 days ago); W J Burke has had zero runners over the past 14 days, going preference is unknown, and consecutive poor efforts make this hard to recommend without more evidence.
runners_data.comment: Making his rules debut after failing to complete in a point-to-point at Dromahane, he faces a stiff task against more experienced hurdlers; the brief break since suggests connections are ready to try him here, but he is up against it in this context.

runners_data.name: Majestic Horizon
runners_data.note: Unexposed five-year-old for P J Rothwell who has placed twice in two hurdle starts on Good ground — both at similar distances; Tiernan Power Roche takes the ride and the consistent placed form on similar going is the main positive, though a win has yet to materialise.
runners_data.comment: Point form has translated well under rules, with a win to his name in recent starts before a couple of placed efforts; third at Downpatrick last time in a bumper, he steps up to hurdles over a longer trip and looks capable of further progress on good ground.

runners_data.name: Newbrook Diamond
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained six-year-old prominent racer with a wide range of form including a place in one of seven Good-ground starts; the headgear (blinkers) is noted, 72 days since last run is fine for the yard, and Elliott's 6/46 14-day record is solid — one to respect each-way even if Good ground has only produced one placing from seven similar efforts.
runners_data.comment: Third at Perth last time, running to form back up to today's distance, and clearly effective over 2m-2m4f on heavy and yielding; first-time blinkers add interest, though he is without a win in his last five starts and remains vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Gavin Cromwell with four placings from five Good-ground runs and a perfect five-from-five in terms of being in the mix; Keith Donoghue is an experienced jump jockey and the Cromwell yard is in excellent form at 9/49 over 14 days — the most reliably placed horse in the field.
runners_data.comment: Finished 5½l third on his hurdles debut at Tramore last time, performing with credit on his introduction to the jumping game; effective on a sound surface and the step up in trip today should suit, with more likely to come as he gains experience over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Tomthescaffolder
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Henry De Bromhead, 50 days since last run, with placed form over hurdles on Good and Soft; Darragh O'Keeffe is a high-class jump jockey and De Bromhead's 6/44 14-day record is strong — the combination of a top jockey, in-form yard, and a hold-up style that suits a contested pace makes this one of the most interesting runners.
runners_data.comment: Fourth on his hurdles debut at Clonmel, beaten 8l but performing to his level over today's sort of trip on a sound surface; the short break since should not be an issue and there is a case for him at this level.

runners_data.name: Nile Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade-in-finish flag and three consecutive last-place finishes on Heavy ground; 139 days off the track and now dropped in weight to 161lbs, but the form is deeply uninspiring and the going switch to Good is an unknown — hard to be positive.
runners_data.comment: Trailing throughout at Gowran Park on his most recent outing, beaten well off the pace, he returns from 139 days off having yet to show anything useful under rules; hard to fancy until he gives a better account of himself.

runners_data.name: Magical Sal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed once in four Good-ground starts but has also pulled up in recent form; 19 days since last run with Gavin Brouder up for a trainer without recent winners — the form string of 63P-57 suggests inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Downpatrick last time in a mares' bumper, falling short of her previous form; makes her hurdles debut here and the step up in trip could help, though she needs to bounce back to her better level to feature.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade-in-finish flag and a largely poor recent form string (2000-5); placed twice on Good ground from five similar-going runs but the heavy defeats in between are concerning, and 49 days since last run for a small trainer.
runners_data.comment: Showed ability on her hurdles debut at Kilbeggan despite finishing fifth and being comfortably held; rated second on these figures and the step up in trip from 2m1f could bring out more, with this distance potentially a better test for her.

runners_data.name: Rosie Brown
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fade-in-finish flag and a placed effort over further on Good ground (3rd of 9 at 18f) as her best effort; Josh Younge claims 7lbs but the overall form profile — including a 22nd-place finish — makes this very difficult to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well off the pace at Punchestown last time, she has shown little over hurdles to date and remains hard to back with confidence; the going is familiar and an earlier third suggests some ability, but she needs to improve markedly to feature here.

runners_data.name: Sea Feliz
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed five-year-old from the Willie Mullins yard with no form on record at all; the Mullins team hits 4/30 over 14 days and the horse is likely to be well-prepared on debut, but the total absence of form data makes assessment impossible — market move will be key.
runners_data.comment: A Getaway mare purchased for 19,000 euros, she is a half-sister to Morricone who was useful at around 2m4f; the trainer's record with debutants warrants respect and she is not without a chance on first appearance if taking to the hurdles.

runners_data.name: Mind Eraser
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old whose last run was a point-to-point 40 days ago finishing fifth; form of 5-44 over hurdles is modest and Mary Ellen Doyle has had no runners in the past 14 days — the point-to-point background is noted but the translation to hurdles is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a maiden point at Tattersalls Farm, beaten 9l, he brings some experience from that sphere to his rules debut; showed ability at 3m in points and could transfer that to hurdles, though the switch to rules is a significant test.

races.paceDynamic: Colwyn Bay and Great Entirely are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner maiden hurdle over 2m4f on Good ground at Wexford, and both are likely to press for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. With Captain Hanley, Seven Towers, Magical Sal, and Newbrook Diamond all mapping prominently, there is meaningful company through the mid-race sections, meaning the race is unlikely to be run at a slow tempo that simply hands it to a closer. On Good ground over this trip at Wexford — a tight, turning track that rewards jumping fluency and sharp positioning — the honest early pace set by two genuine front-runners will compress the field and expose those without the stamina or cruising speed to sustain their effort into the final climb. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with genuine staying ability and a turn of foot for the final hurdles, as the contested lead will likely see the front-runners weakened late, but the prominent racers with class — particularly those with course-going fitness — are also well-placed to benefit if they track the pace without over-committing.

watchPoints.text: Seven Towers has placed in four of five Good-ground starts and Gavin Cromwell is in strong form — if this horse tracks Colwyn Bay and Great Entirely from a prominent position, it is the most consistent finisher in the field and must be respected throughout.

Tomthescaffolder pairs Darragh O'Keeffe with an in-form De Bromhead yard; a hold-up horse over 2m4f on Good ground with a contested pace in front is exactly the scenario this profile needs, and this runner could be arriving late and hard.

Sea Feliz is a completely unexposed Mullins debutant with no form on record — watch the market closely before the off, as a significant gamble would signal stable confidence and upgrade this runner's threat substantially.

Colwyn Bay has a pulled-up on his form string and Dylan Robinson will need to judge the pace carefully — if he goes too hard too soon under pressure from Great Entirely, both front-runners could capitulate before the straight and gift the race to the hold-up brigade.

With 17 runners on a tight Wexford track, traffic and jumping errors are a real risk for hold-up horses; Midnight Musical, Rosie Brown, and Nile Star all carry fade-in-finish flags and may compound the problem if they get into trouble in the rear of the field.

races.name: Clearwater Construction Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Mount Ferns
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for E McNamara, returning 54 days off with a patchy recent form string including a fall; stays this trip on Good but needs cut to be made from the rear in a race that may not truly run to suit.
runners_data.comment: Had been progressing over hurdles before failing to complete at Cork last time, and returns from a brief layoff; acts on soft and good ground at this sort of trip and, while the latest defeat needs explaining, his earlier hurdle form makes him a live contender.

runners_data.name: Grey Gardens
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who gets to dictate on her own terms — Paul Nolan yard in fair nick (1/13 in 14 days) but she has raced out of her natural prominent role at times; Sean O'Keeffe retains the ride and course craft matters here.
runners_data.comment: Raced too freely in the early stages here last time and was beaten a long way as a result; rated second on these figures and clearly effective with cut in the ground over 2m-2m3f, he has shown enough on earlier occasions to suggest he can progress if more settled.

runners_data.name: Lakota Blue
runners_data.note: 354 days off the track is the dominant concern for this Mr McParlan-trained five-year-old; has placed in three of her last four hurdles on Good ground and races prominently, which suits the shape if fitness holds.
runners_data.comment: Drops back to hurdles after a spell over fences, most recently 8½l third in a handicap chase at Downpatrick, and faces a significant test returning from nearly 12 months off; effective over 2m-2m4f, but considerably more is needed here after such an absence.

runners_data.name: Oh So Charming
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy (7lb claim) partners this hold-up type who carries a tongue-tie and has solid sim-going form (14/15); well placed 19 days ago and course form suggests she handles Wexford, but the compressed pace must quicken enough to give her a chance from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Held up at Downpatrick last time, apparently having encountered a bleeding issue, he arrives with a tongue-tie for the first time; capable of running well over this sort of trip on a sound surface, though an inconsistent profile makes him a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: You Done Well
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare fitted with a tongue-tie and pad, placed on Good ground at this sort of trip; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps offset the 163lb burden, but she needs a stronger pace than Grey Gardens alone is likely to create.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated at 120 on our figures, he went close at Clonmel last time, beaten 3l from a mark 1lb lower than today's; effective over 2m-2m4f on soft and good, consistent placed runs give him solid claims, and first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces add interest on a mark of 95.

runners_data.name: Kentucky Bluebird
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Gavin Cromwell with Keith Donoghue up — the high-volume trainer yard (7/41 in 14 days) is worth noting, but this horse is shifted forward on the map because genuine closers are over-stocked; has never won or placed in this grade on Good.
runners_data.comment: Showed a return to form here last time, racing prominently and finishing fourth beaten 6l in an encouraging display; effective around 2m on good ground and she has a solid chance of building on that effort, with the rating on our figures suggesting she is ahead of the handicapper.

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner fresh off a 76-day break; hold-up style, limited Good-ground sim-going form (3/6), and a form string including a fall and pulled-up run — needs everything to fall right from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete at Bellewstown last time, adding to a difficult recent record that includes a fall; effective around 2m with cut in the ground but she has everything to prove at this level after those setbacks, and the break since adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the ride for Anthony Mullins but an 80-day absence and a string of tenth-or-worse finishes at this sort of trip on Good ground make it difficult to be enthusiastic; naturally comes from off the pace though the race shape won't be ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ninth at Clonmel on his most recent start, showing more initiative but fading late having perhaps needed that run after a break; effective at this sort of trip and beyond on heavy and yielding, and could take a step forward now that outing is under his belt.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Flagged as a finisher who fades late, which is an ominous combination with a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo; Liz Doyle representative off 32 days, five-time placer in none of her last seven — the redistribution to midfield reflects the over-stocked hold-up division, not a natural style change.
runners_data.comment: Fifth in her handicap debut at Listowel, beaten 10l but handling the switch to handicap company; effective at 2m and the trajectory appears to be moving in the right direction, which gives grounds for cautious encouragement here.

runners_data.name: Mr Macphisto
runners_data.note: Long-absent (593 days) but has a strong Good-ground profile (15/15 in sim-going) and two wins from prominent-racing style; Eoin Griffin handler, tongue-tie fitted — if the layoff hasn't dulled his edge this is the profile that suits the race shape best.
runners_data.comment: Away from the track for nearly 600 days after exiting at Navan, he faces a major test returning from such a prolonged absence; effective over 2m-2m3f and the addition of a tongue-tie could sharpen him, but overcoming that long layoff is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Dark Berkshire
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell runner back in 19 days, headgear fitted, and flagged as a fader — true hold-up type shuffled forward on the map because of the rear-end congestion; form figures (0897-P) and a string of midfield finishes at this trip on Good make winning unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Consistent at the wrong end of the field and again failing to complete at Downpatrick last time, he is difficult to recommend on what he has produced to date; first-time cheekpieces are the only positive angle but there is plenty of improvement required.

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: S Curling-trained five-year-old with a bleak form string (0/0-00) and fades flagged; Phillip Enright rides off 24 days — a natural hold-up horse shown in midfield by necessity, and nine-race winless run on Good suggests confidence is hard to source.
runners_data.comment: Jumpy at his hurdles at Sligo last time and never involved from off the pace, he has everything to prove having failed to place in his last four starts; usually races in behind and has produced little to inspire confidence in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Mount Hotham
runners_data.note: Nine finishes including four zeros at this class level, returning 33 days off for John Joseph Hanlon; Paddy Hanlon (5) claimed — fades flagged and shifted forward on the map, but recent history at 2m on Good (4/7 sim) has rarely threatened.
runners_data.comment: At Kilbeggan last time, he was dropped off and beaten well, struggling to match strides throughout; seems effective at 2m but has significant improvement to find before becoming a factor in this grade, and the overall form gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Esticky End
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old Dylan Robinson ride for Tom McGuinness; prominent style which suits the race shape behind Grey Gardens, but form figures (R55-7P) and a low OR of 72 suggest getting competitive is the challenge in this company.
runners_data.comment: Exiting at Tramore on his latest start, with a refusal in his recent form, he is in disappointing shape at the lower levels; carries a light weight and acts at 2m, but there is a great deal to find on the evidence of recent runs.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: Fascinating by background — won three times at Dundalk on the All-Weather (flat) but making a hurdling debut for John C McConnell off 287 days (119 flagged); natural hold-up type redistributed forward, and sim-going on turf (5/11) is limited — entirely unexposed over jumps.
runners_data.comment: Performed well at Dundalk last time, beaten 4l in a flat handicap, but faces a bigger ask returning to hurdles where his recent record has been poor; back from a break for a discipline he has struggled with and has plenty to prove in this sphere.

runners_data.name: O'Grady Cracker
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old without a jockey listed, flagged as a fader, and returning 80 days off; only four hurdle runs to date on Good/Heavy with nothing better than a 9th — OR 94 may flatter at this stage of development.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to land a blow at Clonmel last time, unable to go the pace from the rear of the field; stays today's trip and acts on good to yielding, but his form is difficult to assess accurately and a short break adds an unknown element.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's prominent racer returns 51 days off (11 flagged) with two wins in her career; handles Good ground (11/15 sim), has form over this trip, and if fitness levels are right, her naturally forward position could prove advantageous in a slow-run affair.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Ballinrobe last time in a handicap, performing short of her best; handles 2m on soft ground but she has a fair amount to find now facing handicap company and has yet to demonstrate she is up to this level.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Gardens is the one confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and looks set to stride into an uncontested lead, dictating a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m1½f at Wexford. With no other genuine pace-setter willing or able to press her, she shapes to roll along at her own rhythm, creating a falsely run or at least steady-tempo contest that will compress the field and limit the premium on class alone. That dynamic — a lone leader with cover throughout and a likely injection of pace from the second circuit — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield racers with tactical versatility and the jumping fluency to pick off the leader when the tempo lifts. Several runners including Kentucky Bluebird, Glendine Billy, Syosset and Cinnabar Moth hold up naturally but are shown further forward on the map because the field carries far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — in practice, Oh So Charming, You Done Well and Mount Ferns are the genuine closers, while Mr Macphisto, Lakota Blue and Barrogstown Girl are best placed to slot in behind Grey Gardens and exploit the controlled pace.

watchPoints.text: Grey Gardens — watch her jumping at every flight; if she fiddles a hurdle or is headed before the straight, the entire race shape collapses and held-up runners could close much faster than the scenario probabilities suggest.

Mr Macphisto — 593 days off the track is an extreme absence; if he moves fluently in the early exchanges and travels well behind Grey Gardens, he becomes dangerous, but any sign of rustiness will confirm he needs the run.

Syosset — completely unknown quantity switching from All-Weather flat racing to hurdles after a near-nine-month layoff; if she travels with unexpected fluency she could be massively underestimated by the market, but the risk of an early exit is equally real.

Lakota Blue — the 354-day absence is the key watch-point pre-race; if she moves well in the paddock and McParlan deploys her prominently from the off, she is the dark horse who could benefit most from a compressed, steady pace run to suit front-end types.

Oh So Charming and You Done Well — both need the pace to genuinely quicken off the final bend to get involved; if the tempo remains flat all the way to the last, neither is likely to get a clear run from the rear in a 17-runner field, and any scrimmaging late would hurt them most.

races.name: Clearwater Construction Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Mountain Port
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after a full year off (365 days), wore tongue-tie last time; good-going form reads 1W1P from eight runs on the surface but the lengthy absence and pattern of finishing mid-pack make this a watch-and-see return rather than a confident play.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a lengthy absence and unplaced in his last four; beaten 19 lengths on his Flat debut at Tramore last time, where a slow beginning compounded his problems. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces offer little reason for optimism — hard to fancy ranked last on our figures.

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: Returned to winning ways 37 days ago over 17f on Good ground and jockey Shane O'Callaghan claims 3lb; best form on Good and the recent winner's certificate on this trip is the most relevant recent evidence in the field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here by four lengths last time, held up to good effect, but now operates off a mark 9lb higher. Proven on this course, distance and going, and clear at the head of our ratings. Trainer's current form is a mild concern but the overall profile demands respect.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes over on this horse which won over 17f on Good ground earlier in the season; a hold-up type who is suited by the distance and going, his 5-horse form string contains a run that suggests he can sustain a finish when the pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time, though interference from a faller left him with no chance to get competitive and the bare margin does him a disservice. He steps back 1lb on a surface that suits, effective between two and two-and-a-quarter miles. Rated second on our figures with a clear chance here.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who was placed over 17f on Good ground 32 days ago; Josh Williamson's 5lb claim helps at the weights, and a step back from the heavier surfaces that produced his worst efforts is a positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Beaten six lengths at Listowel last time in a run that reads better than it looks — she was never in an ideal position throughout. Handles this distance and going and is showing a return to form. Yet to score in her last five, but not without a shout here.

runners_data.name: My Mate Tony
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher who fades in the final stages; has tongue-tie on and the concern flag around the finish is backed up by a form string showing no wins or places — not a horse to rely on for the closing stages of a 2m1½f contest.
runners_data.comment: Last seen being pulled up at this course, and his recent form shows little; inconsistent throughout his last four starts. Handles the distance and going and will likely be held up — first-time tongue-tie might help him settle. Needs to show he can complete before he can threaten.

runners_data.name: Hatfield Hammer
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and primary pace-setter for this race; Paul Nolan's string is in good form (3/13 over 14 days), but a STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 signals he is operating slightly out of his most comfortable role and his chance in shapes that depend on this position should be tempered accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Sixth at Clonmel last time, fading in the final stages after returning from a break; the effort was in keeping with his form profile and he should be sharper for it now. First-time cheekpieces applied; handles today's distance and going and usually settles well held up. A consistent sort who merits respect.

runners_data.name: Baby Fish
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell has been in prolific form (4/66 in 14 days) and this horse is rated 92, but a finish-fade flag and only 2 from 5 sim-going runs give cause for caution; unknown true style and the 56-day break is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Eighth at Downpatrick last time, making errors throughout and beaten some way; she is learning on the job over hurdles. Off a short break and trying first-time tongue-tie, which may help her focus. Handles today's going over two miles and the handicap mark could be kinder once she settles.

runners_data.name: Hidalgo Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has finished placed 3 times in 15 good-going runs; his trainer is in form (1/7, 14 days) and he ran second on similar ground 26 days ago — however, he is a genuine hold-up type who will be hemmed in further than ideal and the STYLE_FIT rating reflects the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with renewed purpose at Punchestown last time, runner-up beaten four lengths off a mark 1lb lower than today's; he has been reliable without ever getting his head in front. First-time tongue-tie and blinkers added for a gelding effective at this distance and going. Rates a genuine danger on these figures.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher at the bottom who wears a hood; his 60-day absence, all-zero recent form and finish-fade flag compound the positional difficulty — genuinely needs to close from the rear but will be trapped in the mass of horses displaced from their natural spots.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in each of his last four starts and well down the field at Down Royal most recently, where he raced too freely throughout. Wears the hood again today off a short break; usually held up but the keenness shown last time makes him hard to trust. Difficult to fancy on these figures.

runners_data.name: Bella Union
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old but operating at career-high consistency, winning over 17f and 18f on Good ground in recent starts; Darragh O'Keeffe is a major jockey upgrade and the horse's prominent style means he is one of the very few in this field who will actually achieve his natural racing position.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins before last time have him in good heart, and he put in a solid effort as runner-up beaten 11 lengths from the same mark he carries here. Proven at this distance and going; first-time cheekpieces added. A horse in fine form who looks a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Davitts Quay
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with only three starts and a limited Wexford profile; the finish-fade flag, a 74-day break and only 2 from 3 on Good ground mean this is a horse that needs everything to go right in a field of 17, and it will not get its preferred hold-up berth naturally.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Tramore most recently in a maiden hurdle, well beaten in each of his last three starts. He has yet to give any indication of ability, and a short break is unlikely to change the picture significantly. Hard to see him troubling the leaders here.

runners_data.name: Brave Josee
runners_data.note: Four-year-old carrying 153lbs with Kevin Healy (7lb claimer) up; ran second on Good going 24 days ago which is recent enough form, but the finish-fade flag and a 0W record from 6 sim-going starts mean the positional squeeze in this field blunts her best chance.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Sligo last time, caught close home after stepping up in trip, though she now operates off a mark 4lb higher. First-time hood applied; effective over today's distance and handles soft ground, usually settles well when ridden patiently. Must find more to feature here.

runners_data.name: Doyen Og
runners_data.note: Carries the lowest weight allocation and wore blinkers; a 34-day break on the back of a pulled-up run, with a form string showing a steady decline from his 3rd and 4th-place finishes, and the compounded finish-fade flag make this an awkward proposition even in his fringe scenario.
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete at Listowel on her latest start and has been inconsistent throughout her recent runs, with a couple of well-beaten efforts either side of that. Blinkers applied for the first time; she handles today's distance. Yet to score in her last five and the profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Dual blinkered hold-up type who has pulled up twice in recent starts; Denis Gerard Hogan sends one in fair form (3/20 over 14 days), but 4 of 5 finishing positions in double-digits and a PU-heavy form string make this one of the most vulnerable horses in the race.
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete at Sligo latest and has shown little consistency across his recent starts. The trainer's yard has landed 2 of the last 9 runnings of this race, which offers mild encouragement; blinkers tried for the first time. Effective at two miles but the form gives little reason for confidence.

runners_data.name: Bob The Builder
runners_data.note: Returning after 308 days (last run was a pulled-up effort 47 days into a longer break); all five recorded runs on Good ground have produced finishes of 5th-or-worse and the seven-year-old shows a pattern of contesting longer trips — this 17f test may be too sharp on comeback.
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Loughrea last time, beaten three and a quarter lengths and unable to reach his best level; he has finished in the minor placings repeatedly without ever getting competitive at the business end. Effective at today's distance and beyond, but needs considerably more to feature here.

runners_data.name: Notmiwadi
runners_data.note: Four-year-old without a jockey listed at time of writing and absent for 277 days; connections are John C McConnell (1/30, 14 days) and the horse has never finished better than 7th in five Good-going runs — the absence length is the most immediate flag.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Roscommon on her latest start in a maiden hurdle, beaten some way and unable to get involved at any stage; she now returns from 277 days off the track. A switch into handicap company may unlock some improvement, though a trainer in poor current form adds to the doubts. Hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Out Moll's Gap
runners_data.note: All five historical runs have produced finishes outside the top ten, including three on Good ground; a 78-day break and a string of PUs on recent form means this mare is another who will be lost in the hold-up mass and offers very little to recommend her on form.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Limerick on his most recent outing in a handicap hurdle, and his last four starts include two non-completions; he has offered little of note. A short break has been taken but the form gives little basis for confidence, ranked towards the bottom of our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Hatfield Hammer is the sole confirmed front-runner and, in a field of 17 where the pace data shows a consistently Good surface throughout the card, he is likely to control this from the front without serious pressure from a genuine rival — Bella Union will track closely in a prominent position but is not a true pace rival. The bulk of this field is made up of hold-up horses who will be unable to secure their natural position, meaning the pace is effectively set by one horse at a sustainable, unhurried tempo. With Hatfield Hammer dictating a measured rhythm, the race sets up for those who can travel prominently or just off the leader rather than true closers, as ground-savers who sit second or third will avoid the traffic congestion that will engulf the bulk of the midfield and rear. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural position, and Hidalgo Des Mottes, Brave Josee, Sneddy Eddie, Doyen Og, Davitts Quay, Bob The Builder, Backinabit, Notmiwadi and Out Moll's Gap are all genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield on this map — Bella Union and Hatfield Hammer are most likely to actually secure the prime prominent positions. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or in a close-tracking role who can produce a controlled, flat-out finish from 2-out, not those relying on a true late burst from far back in the field.

watchPoints.text: Bella Union (Darragh O'Keeffe) is the one horse guaranteed to track Hatfield Hammer in a prominent position — watch whether she is able to sit on the leader's shoulder from the start, because if she does, she controls her own fate entirely.

Kilt is the most in-form horse in the hold-up group with a recent win over an identical trip on Good ground — watch how Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claim) manoeuvres through the congested midfield from three out, as a clean run could bring him dangerously close.

With 17 runners, falls and interference at hurdles are a live risk — watch for any incident at the second-last where a compressed, slow-starting hold-up group will be bunched together and jostling for a racing line.

Hatfield Hammer's stamina at 2m1½f on Good ground is worth monitoring as the race develops; if he has gone too fast into the back straight, a sudden deceleration entering the home turn could cause a violent concertina effect through the entire field.

Notmiwadi has no confirmed jockey listed — watch for any late booking or withdrawal declaration, as a jockey change at this level on a horse absent 277 days can be a significant market signal either way.

races.name: Curracloe Beach Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Benner Wenner
runners_data.note: Lightly raced De Bromhead five-year-old with only a single run on Good ground; form figure of 8 shows no obvious profile, and the noted tendency to fade in the finish is a concern over 3m½f in maiden company.
runners_data.comment: Held well beaten on hurdle debut at Ballinrobe, he makes more appeal here with scope to progress for a top yard; whether he can do so promptly after that uninspiring introduction is the key question.

runners_data.name: Doctor Elvis
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott, always a combination to respect; placed on Good and Soft, consistent form string of 4220-2 suggests he stays and competes, and the 3m½f trip stretching his stamina is the key query at OR 117.
runners_data.comment: Second beaten 5 lengths at Cork on his latest outing, he has shown consistent form at 2m-3m on soft and good ground; first-time blinkers add an extra angle and the consistent placing record makes him the clear standard-setter.

runners_data.name: Glenary Prince
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's other runner with Mike O'Connor up; placed last time on Good ground over 2m4f which is encouraging for this step up in trip, and OR 120 marks him as one of the leading contenders on handicap terms.
runners_data.comment: Fourth beaten 18 lengths at Punchestown when stepped up to 3m, he shaped as though finding that longer trip to his liking and handles today's going; some further progression is needed to get fully involved.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Lights
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing hold-up type from a small Christie yard with a minimal strike rate; only recent run was a pulled-up effort over 2m3f on Good, making this 3m½f test a significant unknown.
runners_data.comment: Last seen being pulled up at Punchestown, he faces a stiff task as the lowest-rated runner in this field and a substantial step forward is required; first-time cheekpieces are fitted, which at least provides a small change of gear.

runners_data.name: Spill A Drop
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap and hood, completely unknown going preference, and the form reading of F1-4P shows wildly inconsistent profile; Calum Hogan claims 5lb which eases the weight burden slightly, but the unpredictability here is high.
runners_data.comment: Effective at 3m in points and has landed a win in that sphere, he comes here needing to bounce back from pulling up most recently; first-time cheekpieces are applied under rules and there is enough to work with if he responds.

runners_data.name: The Boysofairhill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who sets the pace for the field; on Good ground his last three runs all ended in mid-pack finishes, and his fading tendency means the question is not whether he leads but how long he can sustain it over this extended trip.
runners_data.comment: His most recent hurdles start at Sligo left plenty to be desired, though he brings a win from his point career at 3m; the challenge now is translating that ability to hurdling, where he has so far struggled to show his best.

runners_data.name: Young Doran
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's five-year-old ran a solid second over 2m6f on Good at a previous start — that form profile is directly relevant here; Tiernan Power Roche takes the ride and a horse with one run and a placed effort is worth treating seriously.
runners_data.comment: Second beaten 6 lengths on debut at Ballinrobe, he handles 2m6f on good ground and looks set to improve on that initial effort; rated second here, the one concern is the trainer's very quiet recent spell.

runners_data.name: Bridgie Browne
runners_data.note: Sean O'Keeffe partners this Martin-trained mare who is a genuine hold-up type by nature — form of 8-0 is modest, but she carries a 7lb weight advantage at 151lbs and will be coming from off the pace regardless of where she maps on the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on both her recent bumper appearances, she now makes the switch to hurdling with first-time tongue-tie applied, suggesting connections see room for improvement; that bumper form leaves her something to prove, but the discipline change could work in her favour.

runners_data.name: Im A Dream Twister
runners_data.note: Amateur rider Mr B T Stone on a horse with two point-to-point pulls as recent form and completely unknown going and style profile; the step from pointing to hurdles over 3m½f is a large ask with no public form to reference.
runners_data.comment: Little to recommend her on two recent starts, both ended without completion, she has yet to show any discernible ability and arrives from a short break looking a difficult proposition to side with.

runners_data.name: Mambo Du Large
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday, which is an extraordinary turnaround for a 3m½f maiden hurdle and the primary concern here; form of P70 is weak, and even if physically fine, the quick back-up over this trip is a significant physical test.
runners_data.comment: Prone to errors on hurdle debut at Clonmel where he was well beaten, this gelding is likely to need more time to develop; returning only a day later compounds the challenge and he makes limited appeal.

runners_data.name: Mayo Shirocco
runners_data.note: Long absence (229 days since a point, 445 days on the flat) is the headline flag; that said, placed twice on Good ground in hurdles and has the trip profile, so if fit after the layoff this hold-up type could emerge as a quiet threat in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Third in a mares point most recently, she handles 3m well enough but her form figures offer no standout effort and more improvement is required if she is to trouble the principals here.

runners_data.name: Pacy Macie
runners_data.note: Unknown going suitability, amateur rider Mr B J Walsh, and a form string of 52P- ending in a pull-up; no clear evidence of stamina for 3m½f, and the OR 120 mark is shared with most rivals meaning no weight relief.
runners_data.comment: A pulled-up effort in a maiden point at Toomebridge on her most recent start, she now makes the transition to hurdling for the first time; there is some point form at 3m to call on, but much improvement is still needed under rules.

runners_data.name: Talas Kera
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type by style whose real position will be at the back of the field despite the midfield mapping; OR 79 stands well below every rival and the competitive ceiling here is a concern, even if Eoghan Finegan claims 5lb.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a mares hurdle at Kilbeggan on her most recent start, she handles today's going and has form at 2m; inconsistency has been a hallmark, however, and her varied record leaves her difficult to rely on.

runners_data.name: Vangaway
runners_data.note: Three runs on Good ground have produced finishes of 11th, 14th and 11th — the consistency of poor performances on this exact going type is a significant negative flag, and the fade tendency compounds an already thin profile.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well down the field at Punchestown most recently, racing without threatening from behind the leaders throughout, her three recent runs have all ended in unplaced finishes and she makes limited appeal here.

races.paceDynamic: The Boysofairhill is the confirmed lone front-runner in a 14-horse field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to pressure him through this 3m½f trip on Good ground at Wexford — a track where establishing an uncontested rhythm from the front is a significant advantage. With a tendency to fade in the finish, the key question is whether his lead turns into a winning margin before the tank empties, or whether the proximity of prominent horses like Doctor Elvis and Young Doran catches him out in the closing stages. Glenary Prince and Young Doran, both natural prominent racers, are best placed to sit just off the pace and strike when The Boysofairhill tires, making the prominent-to-handy profile the primary beneficiary of this shape. Bridgie Browne and Talas Kera are genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is crowded; of the true front-runners and prominent types, The Boysofairhill, Doctor Elvis, Glenary Prince, and Young Doran are most likely to actually secure their natural positions.

watchPoints.text: The Boysofairhill's finishing stamina is the race's hinge point — if he begins to tire before the last flight, Doctor Elvis and Young Doran are both positioned to pounce and the entire race shape pivots on this moment.
Mambo Du Large ran just one day ago; watch for any signs of sluggishness or distress early in the race that would confirm the quick turnaround has taken a physical toll over this demanding 3m½f trip.

Mayo Shirocco returns from a 229-day absence off pointing; if connections have him spot-on, the hold-up profile and Good-ground placed form make him potentially dangerous, but fitness on return is unverifiable until race-day.

With three runners (Spill A Drop, Im A Dream Twister, Pacy Macie) carrying unknown going preferences and lightly raced flags, there is above-average volatility in this field — one of these unknowns performing to an unexposed ceiling could disrupt the expected order.

Glenary Prince and Young Doran both raced over shorter trips in their last starts; watch how comfortably each travels through the first two miles, as the step up to 3m½f will sort out those with genuine stamina from those who are only guessing at the trip.

races.name: Slaney Valley Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Cinammon Roll
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old won twice over 20f+ on Good ground and holds strong course form, but a 272-day absence is a significant concern; natural front-runner who cannot get that role here and will race further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Progressive until his most recent outing when well held up in grade in a handicap hurdle, he now steps into chasing after a lengthy absence in first-time cheekpieces; effective at 2m4f-3m, the discipline change is the key question here.

runners_data.name: Coyote Spirit
runners_data.note: Returned 18 days ago for Elliott and ran flat in sixth — the freshness angle is gone and the redistribution to midfield is a genuine problem for a horse who wants to be on the pace; only one win from 12 runs on similar going tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Struggling badly with his fencing at Kilbeggan last time in a beginners' chase when left behind by the pace and well beaten, he clearly needs to improve his technique over the bigger obstacles; effective at 2m4f, first-time cheekpieces are fitted.

runners_data.name: Donnie Devito
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's consistent placer has been placed nine times from 15 starts on Good ground, but returns from 218 days off and has never won over this trip; wants to race prominently but will have to find room in a congested early order.
runners_data.comment: Third in a beginners' chase at Thurles most recently when a shorter trip than ideal worked against him, he is effective at 2m4f-3m; returning from a lengthy break in first-time tongue-tie, he can go well if at his previous level.

runners_data.name: Duke Silver
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the mount for Joseph O'Brien and this horse has winning form over 24f on Good, but a hat-trick of defeats including a 12th last time suggests a horse out of form; another natural prominent type squeezed into midfield, which further complicates a recovery mission.
runners_data.comment: Third in a Listed hurdle at Punchestown on his most recent outing, this generally progressive sort is effective at 2m4f-3m on decent ground and makes his chase debut here; off a short break, he rates a serious danger.

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained, Sean O'Keeffe up, with placed form over this sort of trip on Good and a return to headgear — one of the few promoted types not redistributed, so crucially retains its natural prominent position and can travel just off the pace from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Third on his chase debut at this venue in a beginners' chase, back on better going, he has shown an aptitude for fences and handles 3m on decent ground; first-time tongue-tie is applied and the stable has a strong record in this contest.

runners_data.name: Fillyoureye
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes partners this Mullins runner who unseated last time and pulled up on a previous start — jumping reliability is the primary concern in a beginners' chase; holds a win on Heavy and a place on Soft but Good form reads as three from nine.
runners_data.comment: After unseating in a beginners' chase at Punchestown on his most recent outing, he is worth another chance over fences having shown he handles 3m with cut; the stable has a strong record in this race and he remains a live danger.

runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: Showed smart form winning twice over 20-21f on Good ground and is trained by McConnell, who sends runners out ready; headgear note (hg:h) and a 33-day break are neutral, and as a genuine prominent type who keeps its position in this analysis, the race shape sets up well for a bold show.
runners_data.comment: Useful novice hurdler last season who showed a preference for making the running, he was last seen pulled up in a beginners' chase and needs to improve over the bigger obstacles; first-time hood is applied as connections look for a more settled performance.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's eight-year-old has not won or placed on Good ground in five tries — a telling stat — and returns after 159 days; a natural front-runner pushed into midfield by the congested pace, with a going profile that raises real doubts.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held in a handicap chase at Naas on his most recent outing, he remains in reasonable shape and is effective at 2m4f-3m with cut; returning from a lengthy absence, he needs to pick up from where he left off to get involved.

runners_data.name: Pinot Gris
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's confirmed pace-setter gets an uncontested lead, which is the central tactical fact of this race; however, recent form reads four defeats including a 16th, and stepping up sharply from 16-17f trips to 2m3½f is an unproven stamina test — the role suits, but the form does not scream confidence.
runners_data.comment: Fourth beaten 7 lengths at Clonmel on his most recent chase outing, he has been below his best over fences but his hurdles-form class is clear; the stable has taken this race twice in five years and first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces could bring out a better effort.

runners_data.name: Silent Selector
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade warning who won over 20f on Good but finished eighth last time; needs a strong pace to deliver off the back, which a single uncontested front-runner may not supply — the tactical setup is fundamentally against this profile.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Cork when he pressed on too eagerly on his most recent outing, he handles 2m4f on a sound surface and has a win in recent form; the official mark looks testing though and he needs to settle better to be effective.

runners_data.name: Wing Back
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type returning after 260 days, carrying a fade warning — the combination of inexperience, long absence and a pace map that does not generate the gallop needed for closers makes this a difficult starting point; a win over 18f on Good is the best line but the profile is compromised.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Thurles most recently, left behind by the pace when a more demanding test looked needed, he now switches to chasing after a lengthy absence; first-time hood is applied and he is effective over 2m-2m2f, though expectations must be measured.

races.paceDynamic: Pinot Gris is the confirmed sole front-runner here, likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 2m3½f — a beginners' chase where De Bromhead's charge can dictate every yard without being pressured. Behind him, Eclipse Chaser, Fillyoureye, and Jackson Lamb are the genuine prominent types most likely to actually secure the positions just off the pace, given that Duke Silver, Donnie Devito, Coyote Spirit, Cinammon Roll, and Mickie Angel are all natural prominent racers who cannot all get their preferred slot and have been redistributed to midfield for this analysis. The two hold-up types, Silent Selector and Wing Back, both carry fade warnings and will need a strong gallop to deliver late — which a lone, sustainable front-runner may not generate. This race shape strongly favours genuine prominent racers who can travel just off Pinot Gris and pounce in the straight, as the pace is unlikely to be hot enough to set it up for true closers; this field holds considerably more prominent types than the race can accommodate, so those who fail to secure their spot early will effectively be racing out of role.

watchPoints.text: Watch Pinot Gris's jumping early — if De Bromhead's horse makes a significant error at one of the first few fences, the entire race shape collapses as there is no other confirmed front-runner to fill the role.

Monitor the prominent horses Duke Silver, Donnie Devito, Coyote Spirit and Cinammon Roll competing for position at the early fences — interference between these four is a genuine risk in a beginners' chase with 11 runners.

Watch Eclipse Chaser's jumping — two pulled-up runs in recent history flag a jumping reliability question, and if Mullins's runner makes errors it loses the prominent position that is its main tactical asset here.

Silent Selector and Wing Back both carry fade warnings in a race where the pace is unlikely to be truly searching — if the gallop is modest throughout, watch for these two failing to land a blow despite looking dangerous in the straight.

Jackson Lamb's headgear note (hg:h) is worth tracking in the early stages — if the hood has a settling effect and the horse travels sweetly just behind Pinot Gris, it is ideally positioned to strike; any signs of pulling or jumping errors would quickly change that picture.

races.name: Molloy Metals Recycling Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Harry Des Ongrais
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who needs things to fall right from the rear, but his form string (/3P07-) is deeply uninspiring and 131 days off for De Bromhead's yard alongside Miss S A Carter's 7lb claim makes this a risky proposition; limited sim-going form (0 wins, 0 places from 4 runs) is a further concern.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well down the field on his hurdles return at Naas, he has been short of his best this season and needs to rediscover his earlier level; returning from a break at the foot of our ratings, he makes a difficult case.

runners_data.name: Nouvotic
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner with outstanding Good-ground credentials (4W5P from 11 similar-going runs) but carries top weight of 166lbs, has been off 65 days, and is flagged as racing slightly out of role in this shape — he leads but may lack the comfortable dominance his form suggests in an ideal scenario; Darragh O'Keeffe is a key positive.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts include a 10-length success in a Grade 3 chase at Punchestown most recently; he handles 2m4f on decent ground and returns in fine form wearing a first-time hood, with a hat-trick very much on the cards.

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's booking for Gordon Elliott's in-form string (8/57 in 14 days) is an obvious positive, and this six-year-old has winning form on Good going at around this trip — tracking Nouvotic from a prominent pitch looks his natural position and the trip should suit.
runners_data.comment: A winner of a novice chase at Punchestown by three-quarters of a length last time, he is building confidence over fences and handles 2m4f on soft and good; a top jockey partnership and first-time tongue-tie and blinkers add interest.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for R P Cody who has placed twice on Good at today's distance range; ten years old but still competitive (2nd last time at 2m on Good), and Danny Gilligan's amateur claim (no claim listed but Danny Gilligan is conditional) keeps the weight manageable at 149lbs.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a Listed contest at Ballinrobe most recently, possibly finding the stamina limit on that occasion, he handles 2m4f-3m on a range of going and must rediscover his best; first-time tongue-tie is applied and he remains capable at his best.

runners_data.name: Antrim Coast
runners_data.note: Returns after 279 days off for Gavin Cromwell's yard, which is worth flagging as a major stamina-sapping lay-off for a six-year-old with no win at today's distance; however his consistent placings (four seconds in his last five similar-going runs) suggest he is a reliable if hard-to-win-with prominent type.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five and a half lengths in a handicap chase at Listowel on his most recent start, he is consistent over a range of trips but yet to win in his last four; returning from a lengthy layoff is an additional challenge and there is a frustrating quality about his record.

runners_data.name: Itsalladream
runners_data.note: Paul John Gilligan's yard is out of form (0/10 in 14 days) and this horse has finished 4th or 5th in his last five runs on Good, suggesting consistent but non-threatening form; the 32-day turnaround is fine and Gavin Brouder has the experience to place him, but he needs something to go wrong up front.
runners_data.comment: Consistent around the fifth in recent starts, he looked more encouraging last time when dropped in class at Listowel, though likely to have flattered; effective around 2m on a sound surface, he needs to back that performance up to be a factor here.

runners_data.name: Bridie's Beau
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap and patience headgear (tp) for Cromwell's second string in this race, and a form line of 20P0-P is not encouraging — three failed-to-finish or pulled-up runs in recent starts on Good are a major concern, and Conor Stone-Walsh's claim (no listed allowance) won't paper over those cracks.
runners_data.comment: Brought to a halt in a handicap chase at Kilbeggan last time, his recent form has been deeply inconsistent with two non-completions in his last five starts; effective at 2m4f in cut, first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces offer a change of approach.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: Dylan Kidd's 7lb claim helps offset this nine-year-old's 145lbs burden; the form line (22P-57) shows two strong second places followed by a pull-up then deteriorating efforts, and his best ground appears to be Soft rather than today's Good surface (2W3P on Soft vs limited Good form).
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Kilbeggan most recently in a handicap hurdle, he likes to race in front and is effective at around 2m4f on good ground; first-time cheekpieces are applied but the trainer's cold recent spell is a concern and others look stronger.

runners_data.name: Lisleigh Lad
runners_data.note: Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is an asset for Ms Eleanor Broderick's small yard (0 runners in 14 days), and Lisleigh Lad has an honest record of placings at this distance range on Good; a 3rd last time from a prominent position suggests he is creeping closer, though a win still eludes him at this OR level.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a handicap chase at Listowel last time, picking up late ground in the closing stages, he is in consistent form and handles 2m4f-3m on any going; a fair mark enhances his appeal and he rates a genuine contender.

runners_data.name: Clonshire River
runners_data.note: Strong on form credentials — 1W7P from 13 similar-going runs and a career best of 2nd in a 2m on Good recently — but 275 days off is a serious fitness query, and while his natural style is hold-up he has been redistributed to midfield in this map due to overcrowding at the rear; that dislocation makes him a difficult tactical play.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up three times in his last five starts, he was beaten around three and a half lengths at Sligo most recently off a slightly higher mark; returning from a long layoff in first-time tongue-tie, he has a chance if that level holds.

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: Won at 23f on Good and has genuine class at OR 114, but 112 days off and a last-run P (pulled up) are red flags; his natural prominent style is mapped to midfield here because the field cannot accommodate all prominent types, reducing his chance of finding his groove in a race with this shape.
runners_data.comment: Brought to a halt at Cheltenham in a hunter chase on his most recent start, he handles 3m on decent ground and has a win in his recent form; returning from a break, he needs to reproduce that earlier level to get involved here.

runners_data.name: Vina Ardanza
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature but redistributed into the midfield map because the rear is congested — Josh Williamson's 5lb claim helps on 140lbs but the form line (33P-4U) features a pulled-up and an unseated in recent starts, and 33 days since last run is fine though the Good going (1W1P from 10) is not his best surface.
runners_data.comment: He came off second best at Kilbeggan when unseating on his most recent chase outing, adding to a mixed record over fences that includes a pull-up; effective at 2m4f, there is still plenty to prove before he can be trusted to deliver.

races.paceDynamic: Nouvotic is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger pressing for the lead on these weights and styles, will dictate from the front at a sustainable, honest pace on Good ground over 2m3½f. Ma Jacks Hill, Watch The Weather, Antrim Coast, and Lisleigh Lad are all prominent-running types who will contest the early positions behind Nouvotic, creating a compact, well-strung-out chasing group rather than a chaotic scramble. This is a controlled, single-leader shape: Nouvotic sets a fair tempo that neither burns off the field nor gifts an easy lead, meaning the race will be set up for horses who can travel prominently and pick off the leader in the final half-mile rather than closers arriving from far back. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate naturally — Kings Jet, Clonshire River, and Vina Ardanza are genuine prominent or hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their preferred position in this shape, with Ma Jacks Hill and Watch The Weather best placed to occupy the prominent slots behind Nouvotic. This race shape firmly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who travel within striking range of the leader and have the stamina to peg him back in the closing stages, rather than late closers launching from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Nouvotic's weight (166lbs) combined with 65 days off means he could tire in the final 2f — watch whether Ma Jacks Hill or Watch The Weather are still travelling on his girth as they turn for home, as either could pounce.

Antrim Coast returns from 279 days off and Gavin Cromwell has two runners in this race; watch his market move closely — if well-backed after a near ten-month absence there may be stable confidence, but cold in the market he remains a significant fitness risk.

Kings Jet, Clonshire River, and Vina Ardanza are all racing out of their preferred tactical positions due to redistribution — watch for scrimmaging in the early stages as these horses find themselves squeezed out of their natural slots, which could cause interference or hamper their chances entirely.

Bridie's Beau has pulled up or failed to finish three times recently on Good ground; if he weakens sharply before the straight he could become an obstacle for horses tracking through the field, particularly those held up in the rear group.

The trainer combination of Gavin Cromwell running both Antrim Coast and Bridie's Beau creates a potential tactical split — Conor Stone-Walsh on Bridie's Beau may sacrifice ground to protect Mike O'Connor's Antrim Coast if the stable has a clear first string, worth monitoring in the early exchanges.

races.name: Save The Date 7th August Ladies Day Handicap Chase (0-100)

runners_data.name: A Snow White Park
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up mare for Margaret Mullins and Richard Deegan, with solid good-ground form (7/9 runs OK) and a recent placed effort at 22f; her natural style is rear of field, which suits if the race develops late momentum, though big-field traffic is a risk.
runners_data.comment: Second in a beginners chase at Tramore on her last start, beaten 13 lengths, and has shown she handles this going and trip. Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14th on our figures, the hurdle record offers more than the chase form to date.

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: Simon Torrens takes the ride on this consistent prominent-racing nine-year-old with outstanding good-ground figures (12/15, 2W7P); well-suited by the 2m3½f trip and likely to secure his natural position close to the pace — a key beneficiary of the even gallop.
runners_data.comment: A reliable mare who placed second in a handicap hurdle at Clonmel 28 days ago, beaten 6 lengths on going she handles. Effective over this trip and tries a first-time hood today; holds a fair claim in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Ingenious Stroke
runners_data.note: Mr B T Stone (7lb claimer) takes the mount for Henry De Bromhead, who is in form (T14: 5/40); Ingenious Stroke hasn't run since 1386 days ago but showed smart form with four placed efforts on good ground and the De Bromhead stable angle is the main positive — extreme freshness is the obvious concern.
runners_data.comment: Won a beginners chase at Downpatrick on his most recent start by a length, not fully extending himself at the line, and acts on this going over the trip. Top-rated on our figures, though he returns from a very lengthy absence and that is the key question.

runners_data.name: Temptationinmilan
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type for Eamon Courtney with zero wins or places on similar going across 11 attempts; LR 43 days, stepping up in trip, and the form string (P450-7) gives little encouragement at this level.
runners_data.comment: Beaten out of sight in a handicap chase at Limerick 43 days ago and without a win in his last five starts. Handles the trip and this going, but an ageing, inconsistent performer who is hard to fancy ranked 17th on our figures.

runners_data.name: Giant Haystacks
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap applied, races prominently for Ross O'Sullivan (T14: 2/18); has placed in three of five runs on good ground and stayed 22f well — will likely sit close enough to be involved if he travels, though his record on softer ground is weak.
runners_data.comment: Third in a beginners chase at Tramore last time, beaten 16 lengths, and is developing over fences on ground he handles. Tries a tongue-tie for the first time today; winless in his last five but a danger to the selection at this level.

runners_data.name: Le Malin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a 554-day absence for S McParlan; won at 20f on good ground and has placed form at staying trips, but the layoff and modest good-ground strike rate (5/11) make it hard to trust first time back.
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap at Down Royal by five and a half lengths off this exact mark on his last start, showing the trip suits him on this going. The concern is a very long spell off — 554 days — and he needs to recapture that form on return.

runners_data.name: Sampoet
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for D M Christie, blinkers on, with an exceptional fit to today's conditions (11/12 on good going); LR 20 days, low weight 161lbs, and uncontested lead almost certain — will set the race's entire pace shape and deserves maximum respect for doing so.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a handicap chase at Downpatrick 20 days ago, beaten 8.25 lengths after returning to a longer trip that suits, and handles this going. Tries first-time blinkers today; inconsistent profile means he needs to build on that effort.

runners_data.name: King's Son
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the ride on this lightly-raced six-year-old for Seamus Neville; two placed efforts at 20f on good ground suggest the trip and conditions are right, but the form also includes distant finishes and the hold-up style means traffic navigation in 19 runners is essential.
runners_data.comment: Chase debut produced a return to form at Downpatrick 20 days ago, third beaten 9 lengths over today's trip on ground he handles. Effective at 2.5m and may get further over fences; winless in recent starts but that debut effort is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Sledgehammer
runners_data.note: Races as a genuine hold-up horse but is mapped to midfield given the volume of rear-positioned runners; C W J Farrell has no recent form (T14: 0/0) and the record (15P6-6) is uninspiring — even from a better-than-natural position, the chance looks limited.
runners_data.comment: Out the back and well held in a maiden chase at Downpatrick last time, this point winner still has much to prove under rules. Acts at 3m on yielding ground and is usually ridden patiently, but ranked 18th on our figures he is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Gavin Cromwell (T14: 9/49 — strong trainer strike rate); wears a tongue-pad, placed at 24f on good ground, and the unseating last time is context not form; trainer form is the strongest angle here.
runners_data.comment: Parted company with his rider in a handicap chase at Tramore last time, but had shaped with promise before that. Handles this ground and trip, adds first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and retains potential at 3m — scope for better.

runners_data.name: Ixigreczed
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish on recent starts, and is a true hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by the volume of similar types; the form string (906-00) and soft-ground preference (1W from good) mean this looks very difficult to recommend, regardless of position.
runners_data.comment: Finished out of the frame in a handicap hurdle at Limerick 36 days ago and winless in her last five starts. Effective at 2.5m and handles this going, but has an inconsistent record; first-time blinkers are the angle to follow here.

runners_data.name: Hey Sir
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) for Peter Maher with a light recent history (3 runs on sim-going); LR 63 days with a hurdles prep 40 days ago, tongue-strap fitted — not enough data to assess confidently, and likely needs everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Third in a maiden at Ballingarry on his most recent start, beaten 16 lengths, and has yet to show what he is capable of under rules. Tries a first-time tongue-tie today; ranked 19th on our figures and hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Deadheat
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old returning from 347 days off for S McParlan; true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by redistribution, and the soft-ground form (3/15 on sim-going) contrasts badly with today's good surface — very hard to make a case at this stage of career.
runners_data.comment: Off since a pulled-up effort in a handicap chase at Cartmel nearly a year ago, returning from a lengthy spell away with form trending in the wrong direction. Handles this trip and going, but the layoff combined with that downward trajectory makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Sunwalk
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish flag applies; genuine hold-up type placed into midfield mapping — the form string (PP2P9-) confirms recent struggles and LR 88 days adds uncertainty; the finishing tendency and out-of-role position combine to make this an unlikely winner.
runners_data.comment: Pressed on too hard early and finished out of contention in a handicap hurdle at Cork on his most recent start. A maiden over hurdles returning from a short break, he has a lot to prove making his debut over fences.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old for John G Carr with Josh Williamson (5lb) in the saddle; recent form is eye-catching (44-421) with a win at 24f on good ground, and the good-going record is excellent (14/15) — in-form trainer (T14: 1/1) and seasoned jumper, though age and being pushed forward from true hold-up style tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Downpatrick 20 days ago off a 6lb lower mark and handles this ground and trip. In good form over fences, though he has a higher mark to overcome today and tries first-time tongue-tie and blinkers.

runners_data.name: Party Pack
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap, hold-up horse mapped to midfield; form (7P58-7) and going record (10/15) are not compelling, and J P Flavin's trainer strike rate is quiet — no strong angle to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Out of the frame in a handicap hurdle at Tramore 34 days ago, below his best, and winless in his last five starts. Acts on good ground at this trip, and the stable has a strong record in this contest; still a maiden at this level though.

runners_data.name: Luimneach
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a hood and tongue-strap for Conor O'Dwyer, ridden by Charlie O'Dwyer (3lb claim); LR 33 days, form string (U02P-5) includes a good second at 20f on soft, but good-ground record (10/15) is moderate — the weight pull and amateur claim are the main interest.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a handicap chase at Kilbeggan 33 days ago, struggling with his fencing throughout, and has an unreliable profile. Handles this going and trip, tries first-time hood and tongue-tie; his mark looks fair on hurdle form but attitude questions linger.

runners_data.name: L'Amiral Fromentin
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who ran just three days ago — the most significant flag here; P J Rothwell has no recent form (T14: 0/0), wears a hood, and has placed at 16-18f on good ground, but racing on three days' turnaround over a longer trip with a hold-up style is a considerable ask.
runners_data.comment: Second at this course last time, beaten 4 lengths off this exact mark, but exerted himself too much in the lead early on. Has been in fair form of late and handles this going; first-time cheekpieces fitted today and the quick turnaround of 3 days is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Driveonwill
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Ross O'Sullivan (T14: 4/24) with a tongue-strap; won at 20f on good ground and falls/unseating (U) in recent starts are a jumping reliability concern — if the jumping holds up, the style is perfectly suited to sitting close to Sampoet's honest pace.
runners_data.comment: Coming off a departure at Downpatrick 20 days ago, though he was progressive when winning over fences before that fall and handles this trip and ground. A tongue-tie is fitted for the first time today; a strong danger if he completes the course.

races.paceDynamic: Sampoet is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and will lead from the outset, setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop on good ground over 2m3½f — conditions that suit his record (11/12 runs on similar going). With no rival likely to seriously challenge him for the lead, the pace will be genuine but controlled, creating a race that flows rhythmically rather than explosively, and the absence of a pace duel removes any prospect of the field stringing out early. The prominent trio of Tingarran Express, Ingenious Stroke, Giant Haystacks, and Driveonwill will press into positions just off Sampoet, likely creating a compact front group heading into the back straight. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Sledgehammer, Ixigreczed, Deadheat, Sunwalk, Fr Gilligansvoyge, and Party Pack are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, with Tingarran Express and Driveonwill the most likely to actually secure their natural prominent positions given ability and jockey quality. A controlled, single-pace gallop with a compact mid-race pack and a stamina-testing final climb favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can be produced with a clean run — hold-up horses from the rear face traffic risk and limited room to wind up in a big field.
